To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

oral palonossetron 0.5 mg was non-inferior to IV palonossetrone 0.25  mg for preventing CINV in patients with malignant solid tumours scheduled to receive HEC, and the safety profile of the oral formulation was comparable to that of the intravenous formulation.
oral palonossetron is non-inferior to IV palonosseton in terms of CINV in patients undergoing cisplatin-based HEC.
oral palonossetron is non-inferior to intravenous palonosetrom in the prevention of CINV in patients with solid tumor receiving cisplatin based chemotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new and improved methods to prevent and treat chemotherapy-induced nausea and/or vomiting (CINV), and we are particularly interested in the use of the 5-HT3 receptor antagonist palonosetren.
the development and implementation of a new method for the analysis of the data.
the efficacy and safety profile of oral palonsetron in comparison to IV palonosertorn for the prevention of CINV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oral palonossetron 0.50  mg is non-inferior to IV palonossetrone 0.25  mg, when both are administered with oral dexamthasone for the prophylaxis of CINV.
oral and IV palonossetron are equivalent for the prevention of CINV in patients receiving cisplatin.
oral palonossetron is a safe and effective alternative to IV palonosseton in the prevention of cisplatine-related CINV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oral palonosoteron is non-inferior to IV palonosotern and can be used as a first-line treatment for the prevention of CINV in HEC.
the oral palonossetron was as effective as IV palonosertorn for the prevention of CINV in the acute phase in patients undergoing cisplatin-based HEC.
oral palonosoteron is non-inferior to intravenous palonosetoron in preventing cisplatin-induced CINV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oral administration of palonosetronic can be considered a viable alternative for patients who are unable or unwilling to receive intravenous therapy.
oral palonosoteron may be a good option for the prevention of acute CINV in cisplatin-based HEC.
the oral formulation of palonosetrons has similar efficacy and safety profile to IV formulation.
